lens: story & curiosity: arc, stakes, emotion, pacing, memorable images, plants and payoffs
summary: The spine is excellent. A detective case ('Who taught it?') and a candle clock, where each belief burns for exactly as many years as it was held, turn 80 years of history into one readable device, and the board becomes a network at the end. Most plants pay off over long distances: Widrow's 'Remember him' (2:40 to 31:40), the tall man at the edge of the light, 'Put that in the file', Rosenblatt's 1961 note returning as 'language was the door', 'Who paid for dinner?', and Lenat's 'practically nothing from raw text'. The return to the opening room at 24:15 lands. The deep dives are hands-on (stencil arithmetic, the jug of light, divide by eight). The weak spots are these. Several round-9 script-editor fixes were never applied (L1104, L1517, L1516b, the ch12 order, L0312, L0501). Act 3, from about 27:15 to 31:20, turns into a docket of news items with no human scene. The opening hook is read faster than any other part of the film. Two key questions are planted only as silent cards. Fixing the unapplied story notes would push story and curiosity to about 8.5.
previousRoundCheck: No earlier film-review rounds exist. Of the script-stage story-editor round-9 notes, NOT applied: L1104 'Sensible, then.', L1517 'too', the L1516b answer to the second question, the ch12 reorder (s07 still goes straight into s03), the L0312 Love/Hope/Despair line, and the L0524b Hopfield quote. They are re-raised below.

issues.problem: 'Sensible, then.' pays off the Lenat plant (L0515), but the ear can hear 'then' as 'therefore'. That reverses the irony right after GPT-2 has learned from raw text. This was flagged in script round 9 and is still unfixed.
issues.fix: Change to: 'From the file, Lenat's team: "practically nothing" from "the raw text." It sounded sensible, at the time.' Re-narrate L1104 only.

issues.problem: 'The last word is Hinton's, too.' The 'too' has no antecedent, since L1516 is about the dark lantern. The 2017 quote also sits after 2026 events with no date, so the ear takes it as his latest word. This is the film's final farewell to its quiet protagonist, and it is fumbled.
issues.fix: Change to: 'The last word goes to the tall man, back in 2017.' This ends the epithet thread and matches the on-screen date.

issues.problem: The film reopens the case on a second question at L1303b ('how far will it go, and how fast?') and never answers it aloud. The verdict answers only 'Who taught it?'. An ear-only viewer hears a question at 26:00 and loses it, and the silent STATUS: OPEN stamp does not close the loop.
issues.fix: After L1516 add L1516b: 'And how far, how fast? That file stays open.' (pauseAfter 0.8). Time the STATUS: OPEN stamp in ch15-s09 so it confirms the spoken line.

issues.problem: The emotional peak of Act 3 is 'Rosenblatt's 1961 note, sixty-one years on: language was the door' (ch12-s07). It cuts straight into 'Back in 2021...' and 23 s of one company's founding and funding, and only then does the stampede come. Momentum stalls at the peak, and one lab gets a privileged slot: it is the first thing through the door.
issues.fix: Reorder ch12 to s06, s07, s08 (L1219 only), then s03, with L1219b moved to close s03. Reword L1206 to 'Among the runners, a lab born in 2021: former OpenAI researchers, led by Dario and Daniela Amodei, had founded Anthropic.' Re-fit the s03 and s08 shots and the m16 cue to the new order.

issues.problem: Rosenblatt's most human moment, asked what the machine could never do and answering “Love,” “Hope,” “Despair,” is only a silent card in ch03-s06, during the longest narrated-film hold (about 12 s at minute 5). It is the emotional plant for his drowning at L0409, and the ear never hears it, so his death lands on a figure we have heard joke but never feel.
issues.fix: Extend L0312: '...Dr. Rosenblatt said cheerfully. And what could it never do? “Love,” he said. “Hope. Despair.”' Read the quote lower and slower, with no smile. Cut the ch03-s06 holdAfter by about 5 s to pay for it.

issues.problem: The hook is the fastest-read part of the film: L0102 229 wpm, L0103 217, L0109 248, L0114 249, against 153 overall. The brief asks for an unhurried, distinguished narrator, and the first minute is where a viewer decides whether to lean in. 'Put that in the case file' and 'to a lamp in Chicago' come out clipped where they should hang in the air.
issues.fix: Re-narrate L0102, L0103, L0109 and L0114 with direction 'slower, leave air', aiming for about 150 wpm, or insert pauses inside each line (for example after 'We go back to the war years,'). The existing silent holds in ch01-s05 and ch01-s07 can absorb the extra 2-3 s.

issues.problem: Act 3 pacing, about 27:15 to 31:20 (ch14 plus ch15-s05): the film becomes a docket of current-events items: chips, DeepSeek's cost, o1, the market fall, talent statistics, Bletchley, the hotline, the gap, the Pentagon case, a settlement, a warning shot. It has almost no human scene and no question the viewer is waiting to see answered. L1410 alone packs three ideas into one line ('a struck match... still burns, argued over... That belief burned about two'). Curiosity sags just before the finale.
issues.fix: Give ch14 one held human beat and one planted question. Split L1410 into two lines with a pause: 'For a day, markets bet chips might matter less: a struck match.' / 'China trailing by years? That candle burned about two.' Move 'The chokepoint candle still burns, argued over' to L1418. Cut L1416 (talent statistics) to its on-screen card only, or open ch14 with a voiced question such as 'Does the chip fence work?' that L1410 then answers.

issues.problem: At about 40 words, carrying two limits, a Pentagon designation and a split in the courts, this is one of the densest sentences in the film. It sits in a 37 s shot of iconographic props, so it plays as a news ticker.
issues.fix: Break it into three short spoken sentences with pauses, ending on 'That case, too, is open.' Consider moving L1524 (the settlement) to an on-screen card only, so the shot keeps one through-line: the labs under the same light.

issues.problem: 'WHY WOULD ANYONE CHOOSE THE FOG?' is planted only as a silent 7 s card. The ear first hears the question as its own payoff, L0832 at 16:57, so the film's best explanatory payoff ('the net cut its own... deep learning') lands without a felt setup.
issues.fix: Add a short voiced plant in ch06-s08, for example L0616: 'Put that in the file: why would anyone choose the fog?' (about 3 s). The 7 s silent hold absorbs it.

issues.problem: The Transformer deep dive has one human beat, 'Colleagues doubted it.', and it is flat. The ch10-s03 card holds a better one (Mat Kelcey: 'the biggest incorrect prediction of my life'), but it is silent.
issues.fix: Change to: 'Colleagues doubted it. One later called his doubt "the biggest incorrect prediction of my life."' This voices the verified quote and gives the deep dive a wry turn.

issues.problem: Act 2 opens flat: 'Versailles, 1981. John Hopfield presents a network.' The wry, verified Hopfield quote about nobody remembering the talk (round-9 note) is still unused, and Hopfield's later Nobel (L1502) needs this human seed.
issues.fix: Add L0524b after L0524: 'Years later, he wrote: "I have never met anyone who remembered hearing the talk."' (pauseAfter 0.6).

issues.problem: 'And the tall man? Thirty-six years at the edge of the light. Now, it found him.' pays off the film's longest character thread over an empty desk and a reading lamp. It is elegant, but it is the one place the audience wants to see him. The lamp clicks on after a 37 s shot of shelf exposition, and the emotion arrives cold.
issues.fix: Keep the desk, but on 'found him' let the widening pool reach the tall man's standing silhouette at the desk's rim (the ch04-s08 and ch13-s01 puppet). Hold 1.5 s longer in the m11 swell. Trim about 3 s from the shelf section (the 'speech first' card can stay up without a hold).

issues.problem: Under the closing line L1520, 'Somewhere tonight a lamp is on...', the frames from about 32:43 to 32:48.5 are nearly black. The cursor is barely visible and the hand and match arrive only after the line ends. The film's last spoken image says 'a lamp is on' while the picture shows nothing.
issues.fix: Keep the cursor steadily visible through 'a lamp is on', let the match strike on 'suspicious', and light the new candle on 'new candles', with the flame settling on 'come from'.

issues.problem: The ghost glimpse of the candle shelf and the Wall of Forecasts (about 50-54 s) is too dim and brief to register in the frames. The film's central device gets no visual plant before ch02-s04.
issues.fix: Raise the ghost-candle exposure and hold the shelf beat about 1 s longer, so two or three ghost sleeves of clearly different lengths read before the camera rises to the Wall.

issues.problem: The finale's unresolved mystery ('one lantern is still dark') leans on Anthropic's own findings (the L1504 rhyme-planning result and the 'about a quarter of the prompts' card), and the credit card names Anthropic again. Under the brief's 'no promotion' guardrail, the film's closing question reads as framed by one lab.
issues.fix: In ch15-s08, pair the Anthropic card with one independent interpretability statement from the bible (academic or another lab), or attribute the dark lantern to the field as a whole, so the closing question belongs to everyone.

best_moments: ch02-s04 / L0209: the candle clock is introduced: 'Each belief gets one, burning as long as it was held.' One rule turns the whole timeline into a bar chart in wax.
ch02-s08 / L0220: 'The paper that put it out had Pitts's own name on it.' A perfect sting on the first candle going out.
ch03-s04 / L0309: the Mark I's knobs turning, run as the real perceptron rule, then 'You could hear it learn. I love that.' The narrator becomes a person.
ch04-s05: Rosenblatt's death told through Perceptrons' second-printing dedication, in silence. Restrained and devastating.
ch05-s04: 43 s of lanterns, with the error glowing and the messenger running back down, until XOR solves itself 'By itself.' Then 'The sterile extension, it turns out, was not.'
ch06-s05 to ch07-s01: 'Who paid for dinner?' ... 'Each man lost one bet.' A one-minute plant and payoff with real wit.
ch08-s04: the pierced tin stencil over a cross-stitched 4, its arithmetic summing to 3.88, then sliding everywhere: 'A convolution.' A new way to learn convolution.
ch08-s12 / L0823: the error lantern drops 10.9 points, and the narrator says only 'A cliff.'

ch10-s06 and s07: the jug of light pouring softmax into cups (0.20 / 0.07 / 0.53 / 0.20), then divide-by-eight shown as 'learning freezes' against 'learning flows'. The clearest attention explainer I know.
ch12-s06: back in the opening room, the screen swings open like a door: 'Not a new engine. A new door.' Then the first case-file note returns.
ch13-s01: Hinton physically takes his own 30-to-50-years slip off the Wall of Forecasts, a slip that was planted at 0:52.
ch15-s08 / L1514: 'The board was a network all along.' The case board rewires into lanterns, with one still dark.
L0217 to L1511: 'Remember him.' Widrow, planted at 2:40, returns 29 minutes later: 'He wrote that he never got over it.'
